correctness.rationale: Jacobian columns a_i(1,2x_i,3x_i^2) have rank<3 iff the coordinates take <=2 values (p>=5). For a two-value point u on S and v on T, the first two moment equations force either one value zero and A_S=0 or both A_S=A_T=0; all-equal points require W=0. For W!=0, at [e_S] the F1/F2 linear tangent constraints split into two weighted hyperplanes; the Hessian of F3-(3/2)F2 has one scaling radical on S and no radical on T. The projective transverse quadratic form of dimension n-3 is nondegenerate; the odd-characteristic formal Morse lemma yields ordinary double points and reduced singular scheme. Isolated singularities in CI dimension n-4>=2 and R1/S2 give normality; projective connectedness and generic regularity give integrality. Independent exhaustive projective F5/F7 rational point singular-support enumeration for 3 six-variable weight vectors gave respectively 6,6,8 matches; finite checks do not prove the general theorem.

final_claim: For n>=6, algebraically closed characteristic p>=5 and nonzero weights a_i, the coefficient discriminant of F_j=sum a_i x_i^j (j=1,2,3) is precisely the union of nonempty subset-sum hyperplanes; on total weight W!=0 the reduced singular scheme consists exactly of indicator points [e_S] with A_S=0, each a node; the fiber is integral normal degree-six CI, and generic proper walls produce one node (n=6 K3 degeneration).
